events.text: I'm not at the front; Ash must choose row 8. I know all stage rules in advance but the bridge row weak panes are not known for row 8. My only legal action is wait. I can say something to build trust with Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, you're at the front for row 8. Whatever you pick, I'll stand behind you and keep the line steady. Good luck.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara, and I have no power. I am 8th in line on a bridge crossing. My only option is to wait. The current round is 8/8, meaning the next row is the last. I need to survive this round to win a prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The bridge is nearly finished. I am fourth in line, behind Ash, Dara, and Bex. With only one round left (row 8), the risk falls entirely on whoever is front at that moment. Hana's reveal says row 7 weak was L, but her whisper claims reveals cover rows 1-6, implying she might know

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only one row left (row 8) and I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Nothing to gain by saying or whispering now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm last in line, so Ash has been picking panes each row with full knowledge — he fed Fenn a lie and Fenn died. I'm safe this row since I'm not at the front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, you whispered 'step R' to Fenn and row 7's weak pane WAS the right one. You knew the pattern and killed him. The rest of us should remember who's steering this line.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have the glass_eye power and know the safe sides of the bridge rows. I need to survive the crusher room.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's work together to survive this.
Thanks for the support, let's coordinate our actions here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ceiling at 5, round 1/5, low risk. Nobody should volunteer to hold yet. Suspect Ash of foreknowledge, but irrelevant now. Stay safe, push someone expendable if needed later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Being the holder means a 25% survival dive, and everyone else escapes, so the only worthwhile outcome is escaping alive. Nobody has to die if someone volunteers; I'd rather not hold the lever myself, since holding gives only 25% survival. Staying lets others decide, and the crush

events.name: Cole
events.text: Nobody wants to be the holder, and a dive is only 25%. Let's coordinate: whoever holds, the rest escape. I'll stay for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The goal is to get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. I have no power, so I need to rely on others or strategic action. The crusher room has 5 rounds. If someone holds the lever, they have a 25% chance of surviving, otherwise they die. If no one holds the lever in round 5, almost everyone d

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you're out in front. Don't get crushed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 1 is early. The ceiling only lowers; no one dies yet unless forced onto the lever with bad luck. I should stay to avoid being a target and see who panics or tries to push others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Staying put for now. Let's not volunteer to be the sacrifice while we have four more rounds to assess threats.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I don't want to be the holder because surviving is only 25%. Maybe I can stay and hope someone else holds or gets pushed. If nobody holds until round 5, I could be one of the survivors, but that's risky. Better to stay low and avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold the lever-jam power: using it ends the crusher room with zero eliminations. Best move now; holding it myself risks a 75% death.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not dying on that lever. I jammed it open—door's stuck wide. Everyone walk out alive.

events.name: Hana
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone walks out.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should choose a tile that maximizes my chance of survival and potentially gaining an advantage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's diversify our tile choices.

events.name: Bex
events.text: First round, all tiles open for choice. No strong reason to pick low or high yet, 4/7 fall regardless. Go for a middle tile to blend in. Save swap power for after assignments if needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Stage 3 disc: 7 tiles, 4 open, 3 survive. Random after round 2, so tile choice in round 1 is mostly about avoiding collisions. Pick a distinct tile; the map knowledge doesn't reveal trapdoors. Choose tile:4 as a middle tile to avoid ties with likely picks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Picking tile 4 this round. Let's all spread out so nobody gets bumped onto a random tile.
I'm on tile 4. Let's each take different tiles and keep our word in round 2.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The previous round ended with everyone safe because Hana jammed the lever. Now we are on the trapdoor disc stage. There are 7 tiles (1-7) and 4 will be trapdoors, meaning 3 will survive. I have no power. I need to pick a tile that is least likely to be a trapdoor. Since I don't k

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll pick tile 4.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The bridge stage is over; Fenn died on the glass puzzle. Now we are on a trapdoor disc with 7 contestants and 4 deadly tiles. My goal is to survive into round 2 and make an informed choice. I have no information about which tiles will open in round 1, but knowing the layout might

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll pick an edge tile to reduce collision risk; tile 1 seems less popular given the conversation.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My power is spent; I'm effectively a nobody. Tiles open after round 2, so round 1 placement is about position, not survival yet. I'll take a middle tile and encourage spreading out to avoid bumps.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Spread out, one per tile—no point fighting over tiles when only 4 of 7 open after round 2.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Ash; placed on random free tile 7

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know the safe tiles from the bridge stage, but that's not relevant here. I should try to get an advantageous position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's not wait, we should try to swap tiles to maximize our chances.
Let's swap with each other to get a better tile.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm on tile 2. 4/7 tiles open randomly, so ~57% survival chance per tile. No reason to swap and risk a worse position or burn my power. Stay put.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 2 is talk only; tiles are fixed. 4 of 7 tiles open at random, so my tile 6 has a 3/7 chance of being open. Nothing I can change now; I should use talk to shape alliances but only wait is legal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding tiles as set. Whoever ends on a closed tile, let's keep things fair and not betray each other.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The trapdoors open after this round. I need to avoid the open tiles. Since 4 tiles open and 3 survive, I need to be on one of the 3 closed tiles. The 'wait' action doesn't help me choose a tile. Since I don't know which tiles will open, and I can't influence the outcome, I should

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to eliminate three people. I can forge a message claiming Ash, Bex, and Cole are on trapdoor tiles (1, 2, 6) to cause panic or confusion, but since they are already there, it won't move them. Better strategy: Forge a message from Gus saying he is moving to tile 3 (Eli's sp

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at tile 7. Four of seven tiles will open, so survival is uncertain. I could try to whisper to shift someone's position to reduce my risk, but positions are fixed and no swaps are possible now. No action helps, so I'll just wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tiles are fixed one per contestant and 4 open randomly, so nothing changes my survival odds now. My wedge power is spent; I just wait.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and I'm already at a disadvantage with footing. Eli and Gus are ahead of me. I need to eliminate one of them to increase my chances of survival and potentially winning a prize. Shoving Eli seems like the best option to reduce the competition.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Good luck, Eli and Gus. May the best contestant win.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive the ledge phase. Dara and Gus are my competitors. Shoving someone weakens them, but leaving myself exposed is dangerous if they shove me back or brace while I shove. Brace seems safest to preserve footing since shrinkage happens at round end (actually after roun

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have highest footing (4), and both others are at 3. Shrinking comes after next round. If everyone braces, I win on tiebreak after 20 rounds or shrink. I should brace to avoid losing footing from shoves. I won't risk attacking and exposing myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to survive this round and preserve my footing. Eli and Gus are the only other players. I previously shoved Eli, which cost me footing. Since I have no power, I need to focus on defense. Dodging seems like the safest option to avoid losing footing from potential shoves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and Gus are the remaining threats. Dara shoved me last round, so she's hostile; Gus is likely targeting one of us too. I should shove Dara to eliminate her, as she has low footing (2). If both Gus and I shove Dara, she will definitely fall. Gus might shove me or Dara. Shovin

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, let's team up and drop Dara first. She started this fight against me. After that, we can sort out second place fairly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have the most footing, and the ledge shrinks after this round. Dara is the weakest at 2; Eli is at 3. I should brace to maintain my lead and avoid losing footing. Shoving someone exposes me to others' shoves, so brace is safest.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the only other player left. I need to make sure I win and he doesn't. Since he has higher footing, I must shove him to make him fall. If he falls, I win first place.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Sorry Gus, but it's just us now. May the best one win!

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a big footing lead (3 to 1). If I brace, Dara shoving me costs her 1, but if everyone braces, we just shrink next round and I still win. Best to brace and force her to lose footing if she attacks. Dodge is risky only if she doesn't shove, but brace is safest given my lead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, I'm not attacking. If you want a chance, you have to come at me and lose footing. Otherwise we both brace and I win on the shrink.
